dosing.evidence: Aya was administered orally by gavage at a volume of 10 ml/kg... For 8 consecutive days (days 13 to 20), animals received daily administrations of Veh or Aya (100 mg/kg)

handling.evidence: Methods do not describe a handling protocol prior to testing.

group_housing.evidence: Animals weighing 35-40 g were group housed (5-7 per cage) in polypropylene cages

day_night_flipped.evidence: controlled temperature (22-23 °C) and light (12 h light, 12 h dark; lights on at 6:45 am) conditions... All behavioral sessions started between 8 and 9 am

enrichment_housing.evidence: Home cage described as polypropylene cages; no enrichment items mentioned.

assays.assay_description: Two-compartment CPP apparatus (40×20×20 cm each) connected by a central choice compartment (40×10×15 cm). Phases: habituation (days 1-2), preconditioning test (day 3), 8 conditioning days, postconditioning test (day 12), 8-day treatment, posttreatment test (day 21), Mph reexposure (day 22), postreexposure test (day 23). Test sessions = 15 min of free access; CPP score = time in drug-paired minus saline-paired compartment. Tracked with ANY-maze.

application_type.evidence: Aya was administered orally by gavage... Mph and Veh solutions were administered intraperitoneally (i.p.)

setup_habituation.evidence: A habituation session and a preconditioning test were conducted (days 1-2 and 3, respectively) in which animals were placed in the center of the apparatus with the door open with free access to each compartment for 15 min

setup_restrain.evidence: animals were placed in the center of the apparatus with the door open with free access to each compartment

food_restriction.evidence: Rodent chow... and water were available ad libitum throughout the experiments [in home cage]; CPP apparatus did not contain food

water_restriction.evidence: Rodent chow... and water were available ad libitum throughout the experiments [in home cage]; CPP apparatus did not contain water

time_to_assay.evidence: Twenty-four hours after the last conditioning session (day 12)... Twenty-four hours after the last treatment session (day 21)... Twenty-four hours after the Mph reexposure session (day 23)

sample_size.evidence: Experiment 1: control (n=8), Aya (n=8), Mph (n=8). Experiment 2: Mph (n=32) subdivided into Aya (n=16) and Veh (n=16); n=8 per group for posttreatment and postreexposure phases.

outcomes.summary: Ayahuasca (100 mg/kg, oral) induced CPP in mice, as did methylphenidate (10 mg/kg, i.p.), though Mph CPP was of greater magnitude. Repeated ayahuasca treatment in the Mph-paired compartment blocked the reinstatement of Mph-induced CPP following a Mph priming injection, whereas vehicle-treated animals showed reinstatement.
outcomes.statistics: Exp 1: F(1,7)=5.206, p<0.05 (treatment × compartment). Exp 2: postCT vs preCT t(27)=4.824, p<0.0001; full-phase RM ANOVA F(3,42)=2.828, p<0.05 (interaction); F(3,42)=5.097, p=0.004 (test); F(1,14)=8.578, p=0.01 (treatment); Bonferroni: Mph-Aya < Mph-Veh at PRxT.
outcomes.evidence: Both ayahuasca and methylphenidate induced CPP in mice... Treatment with ayahuasca after conditioning with methylphenidate blocked the reinstatement of methylphenidate-induced CPP

B1_num_measures.evidence: Expression of drug-induced CPP was evidenced by the CPP score (difference between the time spent in the drug-paired and in the nondrug-paired compartments)

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: During test sessions, the time spent in each compartment was registered; reported as totals, no within-session time course.

B3_sequential_structure.evidence: No analysis of behavioural transitions or sequences reported.

B4_ethological.evidence: Only zone preference time measured; no natural behaviours scored.

B5_social.evidence: Mice were tested individually in the CPP apparatus.

B6_cognitive.evidence: Conditioned place preference (CPP) model requires learned context-drug association.

B7_automated_classification.evidence: Movement was tracked using the ANY-maze software (version 5.1, Stoelting)

B8_multivariate.evidence: Univariate ANOVAs and t-tests only; no PCA or multivariate analysis.

E1_environment_type.evidence: The CPP apparatus consisted of two conditioning compartments of equal size (40 × 20 × 20 cm)... connected by a central choice compartment

E2_shelter.evidence: No enclosed refuge described in the apparatus.

E3_bedding.evidence: Floors described as black wooden floor and red smooth floor; no bedding.

E5_enrichment.evidence: No enrichment objects in the CPP chambers.

E6_spatial.evidence: two conditioning compartments... connected by a central choice compartment that was accessible by sliding doors

E7_social_context.evidence: Animals were placed individually in the apparatus during tests.

E8_food_water.evidence: No food or water in the CPP apparatus during testing.

D1_continuity.evidence: preconditioning test... postconditioning test... posttreatment test... postreexposure test

D2_session_duration.evidence: free access to each compartment for 15 min

D3_recording_days.evidence: Recording days: preCT (day 3), postCT (day 12), PTT (day 21), PRxT (day 23)

D4_baseline.evidence: Preconditioning test was conducted on day 3 with data recorded and analysed.

D5_followup.evidence: Postreexposure test performed 24 h after the Mph reexposure; posttreatment test 24 h after last Aya treatment.

D6_circadian.evidence: Each session lasted 15 min; no session ≥6 h.

judge_notes: All three candidates converged on a single CPP assay encompassing preconditioning, postconditioning, posttreatment, and postreexposure phases — kept as one assay per rubric (different phases of same paradigm = 1 assay).
Fos immunohistochemistry was excluded as a non-behavioural endpoint.
B1 scored 0 (1 measure): CPP score is a single preference score derived from times in two zones (rubric explicitly says this counts as 1 measure), agreeing with qwen over glm/gptoss.
application_type set to 'multiple' since within this assay both p.o. (Aya) and i.p. (Mph) were administered.
schedule set to 'chronic' for Ayahuasca because Aya was administered ≥8 days (8-day treatment phase, plus 4 conditioning sessions in Exp 1).
DOI marked null — no candidate provided a verifiable DOI from the paper text.
